summary: Build axis-aligned grid layouts on an m×m grid, for m near √n. Each layout has up to two sizes of merged j×j blocks, and unit cells fill the remaining space. Candidates are ranked by exact sum and the best one that passes a first-fit packing check is returned, with zero-side squares padding the rest

Axis-aligned recursive subdivision: a DP over k×k grids (k = 2..5) assigns square counts to the cells, and each cell is subdivided recursively. Spare squares get side 0, and a fallback splits the unit square into a grid when n is large.

Guillotine-partition DP over an M×M integer lattice: for each rectangle and each square count, it stores the best sum of sides and the split that achieves it. It tries increasing M within the time budget, keeps the best layout, and pads with zero-side squares.

Recursive grid construction: for each n, DP over a k×k grid with one m×m block that is recursively packed, while the remaining cells are evenly subdivided recursively. Zero-side squares pad the count to n.

Dynamic programme over layouts: a j×j grid of cells with an i×i corner block replaced by a scaled recursive optimal packing of the remaining squares, with unused squares set to side 0. Because the block can recurse, this beats the plain grid for n between perfect squares.

Axis-aligned squares only. A guillotine-cut dynamic program on an N×N integer grid, with rectangles split recursively and one square per leaf, gives the best total side for at most n squares for each N. The best N is chosen and the layout rebuilt, with a plain grid as fallback for large n.

Build rows of axis-aligned squares: choose how many squares go in each row, then give each row side min(1/count, remaining height), tallest counts first, which is a fractional knapsack. Axis-aligned guillotine DP on a K×K integer grid. For each K it finds the tiling with at most n squares that maximises the sum of sides, trying several K and padding with zero-side squares. For large n it falls back to a grid with one big corner square.

Dynamic programming over a recursive layout: an L-shaped border of equal squares of side 1/c wraps a smaller scaled copy of the best packing for fewer squares. Leftover squares are padded with size 0. This reproduces the grid for k² and does at least as well otherwise.

Guillotine dynamic programming on integer lattices of several resolutions N. For each N it finds the best way to cut an N×N board into at most n squares with integer sides, then scales to the unit square and keeps the best N. Unused squares get side 0. Take an m×m grid, merge aligned 2×2 blocks into single squares until at most n squares remain (each merge removes 3 squares for a small loss), choose the best m, and pad with zero-size squares. This is a general method, but it does not use rotated squares.

For n ≤ 200, a guillotine-partition DP on a K×K integer grid (with merged larger squares) picks the best grid size and layout using at most n squares, and the leftover squares get side 0. For larger n, a closed-form grid with one merged corner square is used instead.

Dynamic programme over integer-grid guillotine packings of squares in w×h rectangles, with at most c squares and spare squares left as points. It picks the best grid size m and rebuilds the layout from the stored choices.
